resale_co.notes: The City's January 2026 'Selling or Renting Property in Corbin City' fact sheet says in writing that the City does not require any documentation or inspections to sell property. An older March 2023 version of the fact sheet, still linked from the Zoning/Construction and Renting Property pages, said 'The city requires documentation of all inspections' and then listed only county septic, well testing and the State smoke/CO certificate; the newer sheet on the Forms page replaces it. Construction inspections are done by the NJ DCA State Construction Office in Hammonton, (609) 567-3653. The zoning ordinance quoted on the Zoning page (Section 102-21.6) sets a $35 fee for applications for certificates of occupancy and continuing certificates of occupancy, but nothing says one is needed for a sale. Rental units must be registered annually with the Zoning and Code Enforcement officer (rental program, Chapter 64). The 2026 fact sheet is linked from the Forms page as https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YSBEuVwDPovVS3IY5l5guotF43xcQ8Ru/view?usp=sharing; the direct-download address of the same file is cited.

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the NJ DCA Fire Safety portal ('Start Your Smoke Certification Application'): give the application date, reason (change of ownership or change of occupancy), closing date, property block, lot and address, and pay the application fee online. Homes heated by electricity with no CO alarm requirement should also email BFCE_CSDCMAC@dca.nj.gov.

fire_cert.notes: The State DCA is Corbin City's fire code enforcing agency (registry code S) and issues smoke certificates there ('SC' on the July 2026 state towns list). The City's own 2026 fact sheet sends sellers to the DCA Fire Safety portal. Fees are now cited from the NJ Register rule text for N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d) ($45 / $90 / $161) instead of the DCA portal page. The DCA portal page was reworded since 2026-09-30: its earlier intro text (CSACMASPSIL name, e-check or credit card payment, certificate sent by email) no longer shows, so those quotes were replaced. The state fee rule text still names the certificate CSACMAPFEC (including the extinguisher); P.L.2025, c.19 removed the extinguisher from the sale requirement.
